set.approach: Drive the Hinkey Summit Road north out of Paradise Valley to a hairpin corner in an aspen grove, and park there or in a small pullout a little way back. The hiking trail, faint in places, starts at the hairpin and heads east toward the big cleft wall, crossing two drainages on the way to the base. Blue Eyes climbs the large headwall in the center of the Cleft. Walk left of Paiute Pockets and through a narrow slot to get to it. The climbing begins with a rightward traverse along a third-class ledge above a chossy overhang.
set.descent_text: The route is equipped for rappel with a long rope, skipping an intermediate anchor, and a walk off is also possible from the top.

review.notes: Area page: parking and trail, quick walk-off; route page: location, rappel equipment, walk-off. Rope length left out.

set.approach: Drive the Hinkey Summit Road north out of Paradise Valley to a hairpin corner in an aspen grove, and park there or in a small pullout a little way back. The hiking trail, faint in places, starts at the hairpin and heads east toward the big cleft wall, crossing two drainages on the way to the base. Brap Machine Paradise is on the left side of the main cave, a way to the right of The Dream Machine. The first pitch has rap rings on its belay ledge and can be set up as a single-pitch climb.

review.notes: Area page: parking and trail; route page: left side of the main cave, right of Dream Machine. Full descent not stated.

set.approach: Drive the Hinkey Summit Road north out of Paradise Valley to a hairpin corner in an aspen grove, and park there or in a small pullout a little way back. The hiking trail, faint in places, starts at the hairpin and heads east toward the big cleft wall, crossing two drainages on the way to the base. The ramp starts right of the cave and left of Steve; go up it. The upper pitches share anchors with Brap Machine Paradise, and the last pitch links with the finish of The Dream Machine.

review.notes: Area page: parking and trail; route page: ramp right of the cave, left of Steve. Full descent not stated.

set.approach: Drive the Hinkey Summit Road north out of Paradise Valley to a hairpin corner in an aspen grove, and park there or in a small pullout a little way back. The hiking trail, faint in places, starts at the hairpin and heads east toward the big cleft wall, crossing two drainages on the way to the base. Clip the first bolt of Paiute Pockets, then traverse left along the grassy ledge to start. One upper pitch is shared with Paiute Pockets.
set.descent_text: The route is equipped for rappel with a long rope, and a walk off from the top is also possible.

review.notes: Area page: parking, trail, quick walk-off; route page: start by Paiute Pockets, rappel equipment and walk-off. Rope length left out.

set.approach: Drive the Hinkey Summit Road north out of Paradise Valley to a hairpin corner in an aspen grove, and park there or in a small pullout a little way back. The hiking trail, faint in places, starts at the hairpin and heads east toward the big cleft wall, crossing two drainages on the way to the base. Splooty is the single pitch directly below the ramp at the base of Paiute Pockets and John Cena Memorial Route, and can serve as an approach pitch to either.

review.notes: Area page: parking and trail; route page: cliff below the ramp. No descent stated.

set.approach: Drive the Hinkey Summit Road north out of Paradise Valley to a hairpin corner in an aspen grove, and park there or in a small pullout a little way back. The hiking trail, faint in places, starts at the hairpin and heads east toward the big cleft wall, crossing two drainages on the way to the base. Steve starts where Blue Eyes does, but instead of traversing right along the ramp it goes straight up the headwall. It ends at the second-pitch anchor of Blue Eyes.

review.notes: Area page: parking and trail; route page: starts as Blue Eyes, straight up the headwall, ends at its P2 anchor. Rope-length notes in the source left out.

set.approach: Drive the Hinkey Summit Road north out of Paradise Valley to a hairpin corner in an aspen grove, and park there or in a small pullout a little way back. The hiking trail, faint in places, starts at the hairpin and heads east toward the big cleft wall, crossing two drainages on the way to the base. The route starts left of the central cave, near Blue Eyes. It climbs three bolted pitches and then a fourth-class scramble aimed at the notch in the Cleft above.

review.notes: Area page: parking and trail; route page: left of the cave near Blue Eyes, scramble toward the gap. Descent not stated.

set.approach: The wall is in Lamoille Canyon. The route starts at the base by the prominent dead tree and goes directly up the slab to a pair of anchor bolts fitted with quick links.

review.notes: Only the canyon is given as access; route page: dead tree at the base. No descent stated.

set.approach: Take the Hinkey Summit Road north from Paradise Valley toward the pass. Park in the narrow pullout on the road below the wall, or at the summit pass; the walk to the base of the climbing is very short. Basque-ing in the Sun is on the southern summit wall, which is almost its own wall, cut off from the other routes by some poor rock and a mound covered in shrubs. It starts in the lowest part of the prominent wall, a short way to the right of Evasive Maneuvers; the first bolt is just off the ground next to a large two-hand pocket.
set.descent_text: Rappelling the route is the only way down; there is no walk-off. The anchors have rap rings.

review.notes: Area page: parking, only descent is rappel; route page: start location, rap-ring anchors. Rope and rappel counts left out.

set.approach: Take the Hinkey Summit Road north from Paradise Valley toward the pass. Park in the narrow pullout on the road below the wall, or at the summit pass; the walk to the base of the climbing is very short. Belly Button is between Don't Call Me White and MuccLovin. Find the first bolt in a water streak a little above the ground, with easy climbing to reach it. The route leads into the large recessed cave halfway across the wall, or can continue past it to MuccLovin and Time Collapse.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route from any of its stations. A long rope reaches the ground in a single rappel; otherwise use the intermediate rap station, and knot the rope ends.

review.notes: Area page: parking; route page: location, rappel from any station. Rope length left out.

set.approach: Take the Hinkey Summit Road north from Paradise Valley toward the pass. Park in the narrow pullout on the road below the wall, or at the summit pass; the walk to the base of the climbing is very short. From the base of Belly Button, follow the moderately steep gravel trail along the foot of the wall past MuccLovin to reach Das Untercling, which lies between MuccLovin and Lucky Pair a Dice. Its last bolt and anchor are shared with Lucky Pair a Dice.
set.descent_text: Clip the steel carabiners at the anchor and lower off.

review.notes: Area page: parking; route pages: gravel trail order past MuccLovin, shared anchor, lower off the carabiners.

set.approach: Take the Hinkey Summit Road north from Paradise Valley toward the pass. Park in the narrow pullout on the road below the wall, or at the summit pass; the walk to the base of the climbing is very short. From Belly Button, follow the moderately steep gravel trail beside the wall, past MuccLovin, Das Untercling and Lucky Pair a Dice. Evasive Maneuvers is the final route on the wall, at the top of the gravel hill by the foot of the gully, a few feet left of it.
set.descent_text: Rappel from the rap-ring anchors at the top of the route. Alternatively, go left around the corner a few feet to the shared anchor with steel carabiners used by Das Untercling and Lucky Pair a Dice, and lower off there.

review.notes: Area page: parking; route page: location at the top of the gravel hill, two anchor options.

set.approach: Take the Hinkey Summit Road north from Paradise Valley toward the pass. Park in the narrow pullout on the road below the wall, or at the summit pass; the walk to the base of the climbing is very short. From the base of Belly Button, follow the moderately steep gravel trail along the foot of the wall past MuccLovin and Das Untercling. Lucky Pair a Dice sits between Das Untercling and Evasive Maneuvers, and shares its last bolt and anchor with Das Untercling.
set.descent_text: Clip the stainless steel carabiners at the anchor and lower off.

review.notes: Area page: parking; route pages: gravel trail order, shared anchor, lower off.

set.approach: Take the Hinkey Summit Road north from Paradise Valley toward the pass. Park in the narrow pullout on the road below the wall, or at the summit pass; the walk to the base of the climbing is very short. MuccLovin starts between Belly Button and Das Untercling. Its anchors are shared with the top of Belly Button, on a comfortable ledge above and right of the cave.
set.descent_text: As a single pitch, rappel or lower from the anchors with a full-length rope. With a shorter rope, belay your partner up from the anchors and use the intermediate rap station on Belly Button. You can also continue up Time Collapse to the top and walk off or rappel.

review.notes: Area page: parking; route pages: shared anchors, descent options.

set.approach: Take the Hinkey Summit Road north from Paradise Valley toward the pass. Park in the narrow pullout on the road below the wall, or at the summit pass; the walk to the base of the climbing is very short. Time Collapse begins from a two-bolt belay on a ledge up and to the right of the big shallow cave, so get there by climbing MuccLovin or all of Belly Button.
set.descent_text: Walk off: scramble easily up and left to the top, traverse right and a bit downhill to get off the back side, then head north past the big arch to the 4x4 road and follow it down to the parking area. You can instead rappel the route; the rappels finish in the cave and then reach the ground.

review.notes: Area page and route page both give the back-side walk-off; rappel line from the route page (count of three is single-source; rope length left out).

set.approach: Drive northeast past Hinkey Summit on Hinkey Summit Road, then park well off to the side in a wider part of the road. Hike northwest on cattle trails through the sagebrush and a small boulder field to reach the middle stretch of the wall. The first bolt is a short way up, with easy climbing to reach it and a flake near the first two bolts.
set.descent_text: Rappel from the anchors, which have rap rings. The walk-off is shrubby, and it is difficult to reach the top of the cliff while still clipped to the anchors.

review.notes: Area page: approach; route page: first bolt, flake, rappel descent and the walk-off caveat.

set.approach: From the pullout on the Hinkey Summit Road, walk a short way up the road to a pair of cairns on the right marking where the trail begins. Traverse the hillsides north-northeast on the clearest cow trail, crossing Indian Creek about halfway at a spot marked by a stick-and-rock cairn and a large Y-shaped dead snag. Past the creek, follow cow and climber trails along the treeline northeast until Iron Horse comes into view; it can also be reached from the Cleft by a short, easy walk on cow trails. Run-A-Mucca is on the southern side of the wall, around the corner to the right of Yippee Ki Yay. It starts up a juggy water runnel, on the left-hand line of bolts, near where Liquid Gold starts.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route; each station has a two-bolt anchor with rap rings.

review.notes: Area page: trail and Indian Creek crossing; route page: southern side, water runnel, rap-ring stations. Distances left out.

set.approach: From the pullout on the Hinkey Summit Road, walk a short way up the road to a pair of cairns on the right marking where the trail begins. Traverse the hillsides north-northeast on the clearest cow trail, crossing Indian Creek about halfway at a spot marked by a stick-and-rock cairn and a large Y-shaped dead snag. Past the creek, follow cow and climber trails along the treeline northeast until Iron Horse comes into view; it can also be reached from the Cleft by a short, easy walk on cow trails. Yippee Ki Yay is on the steeper, west-facing western part of the wall, which is heavily pocketed. The first bolt is reached by climbing the steeper rock beside the slab, on its right.

review.notes: Area page: trail; route page: first bolt right of the slab. Descent not stated.

set.approach: This is a roadside cliff in Lamoille Canyon. Beyond the girls camp, a roadside pullout lets you walk straight to the cliff. The route is a short bolted line.

review.notes: Area page: pullout after the camp; route page: short bolted route to two anchors. Descent not stated.

set.approach: Park in the large lot on the right side of the road in Lamoille Canyon, just inside the canyon mouth. From the parking area, go straight to the nearest rock on the right. Sidewinder tracks the dark streak left of Unknown Route, on the first rock. The anchors are a little hidden at the top.
set.descent_text: There are no chains at the top. Throw the rope over and walk off the back side.

review.notes: Area page: parking; route page: nearest rock, dark streak, anchors, walk-off back side. Distance from the canyon mouth left out.

set.approach: Park in the large lot on the right side of the road in Lamoille Canyon, just inside the canyon mouth. It is on the first rock out from the parking area, immediately right of Sidewinder.
set.descent_text: There are no chains at the top. Throw the rope over and walk off the back side.

review.notes: Area page: parking; route page: first rock, right of Sidewinder, walk off the back side.

set.approach: Park in the large lot on the right side of the road in Lamoille Canyon, just inside the canyon mouth. The route is on the up-canyon side of the formation. It has chain anchors, and a stick clip for the first bolt is wise.

review.notes: Area page: parking; route page: up-canyon side, stick clip first bolt, chain anchors. Descent not stated.
